findings.title: Small-action edit/delete buttons no longer reach the right edge
findings.body:
`.small-action` is now a flex container, but `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow` (no `flex: 1`). It used to be a block that spanned the full row. Now it only takes its content width.

The edit/delete buttons inside it rely on `button { float: right; }` (line 309). They therefore float to the right edge of a narrow box, not the right edge of the post. For short actions such as "closed 2 days ago", the buttons end up right next to the text. With a long custom message they sit at the far right, so the position is inconsistent.

Any `button` that is a direct child of `.small-action` has its `float` ignored entirely, since floats don't apply to flex items.

Fix: add `flex: 1 1 auto` (and likely `min-width: 0`) to `.small-action-desc`.

findings.title: order() passes the value unchanged to the 1-based legacy box-ordinal-group
findings.body:
The 2009 box spec's `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` only accept positive integers and default to 1. Modern `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negative values.

Passing `$val` straight through has two effects:
- `order(0)` or a negative value produces an invalid declaration in legacy engines, which is dropped.
- `order(1)` ties with un-ordered siblings in legacy engines but sorts after them in modern ones.

The current callers (2 and 3) happen to keep the same relative order. The mixin is now a shared helper, though, so the next caller can silently get different ordering per engine. Emit `$val + 1` for the legacy properties, as Bourbon/Compass do.

findings.title: align-items() emits invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end and a non-existent property
findings.body:
`-webkit-box-align` and IE10's `-ms-flex-align` expect `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. Calling `@include align-items(flex-start)` therefore produces invalid declarations for exactly the legacy engines the mixin exists to support.

Separately, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any IE/Edge version and is dead output.

Only `center` and `baseline` are used today, so this is latent. Fix: map the values for the legacy prefixes and drop `-ms-align-items`.

findings.title: Header right-alignment depends on modern-only flex behavior while float fallbacks were removed
findings.body:
The `float: right` on `.panel` and `float: left` on `.title` were removed. Right-alignment of the panel now depends solely on `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container.

The new `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for old engines. In the 2009 box model, auto margins do not absorb free space (alignment is done with `box-pack`), and children's floats are ignored.

The result is that browsers matched only by the legacy prefixes render the panel immediately after the logo instead of at the right edge. The vendor prefixes therefore give a false sense of legacy support. Either drop the legacy `display` values or add the matching `-webkit-box-pack`/`-moz-box-pack` handling.
